workflow.name: Scene And Set Workflow
workflow.purpose: Load a prepared set, recall scenes during playback, recover from recall failures, and persist session changes safely.

rules: Remain visible while transport is playing.
Keep current scene visible until an applied snapshot confirms the target scene.
Show target scene and apply boundary for pending recall.
Show blocked, failed, and partial recovery states at shell scope and affected scope.
Do not replace or hide the performance shell.
Rows preserve stable height across scene states.
Destructive scene edits require confirmation.
High-frequency recall actions do not require modal confirmation.
Current and pending states must be visually different.
Blocked and failed rows expose scoped reason and recovery entry.
Long names truncate without changing row height.
Accessible name includes scene number, scene name, status, and boundary.
Session load validates before replacing the active live session.
Save and autosave are represented as async lifecycle states.
Autosave recovery files are distinguishable from intentional saves.
Failed load or save does not destroy the current live session.
Partial recall cannot be silent.
Failed recall preserves the last confirmed current scene.
Recovery actions are scoped to affected changes.
Resource resolution links back to affected modules, lanes, or routes.
Recovery validation runs before restore.
Restoring recovery does not overwrite intentional save until performer saves.
Dismissed recovery remains distinguishable from deleted session data until cleanup policy applies.
Validate resources and state before real-time handoff.
Do not mutate current scene until an applied snapshot is published.
Bound pending recall work and reject unbounded command queues.
Persist recallable state only.
Validate resource references before inserting scene into set order.
Mark session unsaved after successful capture.
Read and validate off real-time paths.
Do not replace active live session until validation succeeds or recovery is accepted.
Surface migration, missing resource, and unsupported version issues before apply.
Use atomic or equivalent safe persistence.
Do not block audio or MIDI scheduling.
Failed save preserves in-memory session state.
Snapshot is the UI source of truth for current and pending scene state.
Affected scopes map to shell, section, lane, module, route, or resource surfaces.
The UI does not infer applied scene from click timing.
Snapshot distinguishes intentional save from autosave recovery.
Validation issues are structured and scoped.
Runtime-only state is excluded from persisted scene state.

failurePolicy: Unsupported schema blocks session application unless migration succeeds.
Missing resources mark affected modules, routes, scene rows, and shell summary.
Failed recall preserves the last confirmed current scene.
Partial recall is allowed only when failed changes are scoped and visible.

acceptance: Current scene, target scene, and recall boundary are visible in the shell.
Scene selector shows ordered set scenes and does not replace the performance shell.
Scene recall distinguishes current, selected, armed, pending, queued, applying, applied, blocked, failed, and partial recoverable states.
Pending recall keeps current scene authoritative until an applied snapshot confirms the target scene.
Affected Drums, Synths, Post-FX, and Master FX scopes expose scene-driven pending and failure states.
Session, scene, preset, snapshot, and runtime-only boundaries are explicit.
Session load validates before live application.
Save, autosave, and recovery are async and off real-time paths.
Missing resources, unsupported versions, unavailable devices, broken routes, and failed recalls have scoped recovery behavior.
